# Purpose
The purpose of this specification is to define the functional enhancements and rewrites introduced in Sprint-2 of the Sales Order Re-Write module.
The objective is to strengthen the Sales Order workflow by:
• Introducing structured approval mechanisms (Single, Multi-Level, and Multiple Approval)
• Enhancing delivery management actions (Add, Copy, Split, Delete, Cancel, Close, Reopen)
• Enabling editable delivery updates without revision
• Integrating EDI Buyer PO processing for automated Buyer Order creation
• Enhancing audit visibility through History/Log tracking
• Supporting customized print configurations via Layout Mapping Engine
This document ensures standardized, controlled, and traceable Sales Order processing within the system.

# Solution

## Approval Mechanism

### Single-Level Approval
In Single Level Approval, the approval process works between two users.
First, we log in with the user Rishabh. There by user permissions will set another user as the approver. This permission will be applied based on current development of sales order rewrite in which we are introducing a new permission for sales order.
Info Tooltip (i Icon Behavior)
• On hovering over the info (i) icon, the system should display the following conditions:
• 0 → Document will not go for approval
• -1 → Document will always go for approval
• Limit > 0 → Document will go for approval only if value exceeds the specified limit
• This tooltip ensures user clarity and correct configuration of approval logic.
Sales Order (New) – Approval Configuration Fields
• In the Sales Order New screen, the following three fields should be available as shown in the configuration screen:
• Approval Value (INR)
• Approver(s)
• [All] / Selection Field (User Selection Control)
• These fields will be used to define the approval workflow and threshold logic.
Approval Value Configuration
The value “-1.000 INR” represents the minimum threshold amount from which the Sales Order approval mechanism is triggered.
For example:
• If the value is set to 1000 INR, the approval workflow will be triggered when the Sales Order total value is greater than 1000 INR.
• If the Sales Order value is less than or equal to 1000 INR, the approval process will not be triggered.
• In case of 0, no approval will work.
This configuration allows the system to control and trigger the approval workflow based on the Sales Order amount threshold.
After creating a Sales Order and clicking on Confirm, a pop-up message appears for approval. The Sales order is then sent for approval to the assigned user, which can be verified in the Sales Order section.
From Other user account: Click on the Home icon -> Approval Centre -> Sales Order –> Pending Approval. Here, the pending Sales Order will be visible.
From this section, the user approves the Sales order
Once approved, the Sales Order status becomes Confirmed, and this can be verified from the Sales Order List.
Document Approval Screen Behaviour
• In case of New Sales Order (Purchase Order from Buyer):
• The document will be displayed as “Sales Order” in the Document Approval Centre.
• On clicking the OC Number (Document Reference):
• If the record belongs to New Sales Order, the system will open the New Sales Order screen.
• If the record belongs to an existing/old flow, the system will open the existing Purchase Order screen.
Status Display
The Sales Order status will be clearly visible in the system, such as:
• Pending Approval
• Approved / Confirmed
• Rejected
The system will also display:
• Name of the Approver
• Approval / Rejection Status
• Approver Comments
• Date and Time of Action
This ensures complete visibility and tracking of the approval process.
NOTE:
All remarks entered during the approval process will be saved and updated in the History tab for tracking and audit purposes.

### Multi-Level Approval
In the case of Multi Level Approval.
Admin -> Company Setup -> Multi level approval Settings -> Sales Order Check list.
Setting Enhancement:
• Introduce a new document name “Sales Order” in the Multi-Level Approval Settings.
• This will be available in addition to “Purchase Order From Buyer” as shown in the screenshot.
Approval Flow Chain:
Rishabh (Sales Order Creator) → 1st Approver (assigned by Rishabh) → 2nd Approver (assigned by 1st approver and set as Final Approver)
After enabling this setting, the approval flow works in multiple stages.
First, we log in with the first user Rishabh and create the Sales order.
Rishabh assigns second user (Nishu) as the first approver, same as done in the Single Level Approval process.
After confirming the Sales Order, a pop-up message appears, and the Sales order is sent for approval.
Next, we log in with second user (Nishu).
From Second user (Nishu’s) account:
• Click on the Home icon
• Go to Approval Centre
• Open Sales Order – Pending Approval
Second user (Nishu) approves the Sales Order.
After second user (Nishu’s) approval, the Sales Order does not get confirmed yet. It moves to the next level of approval.
Second user (Nishu) assigns WFX Admin as the final approver.
Now, we log in with WFX Admin.
From WFX Admin’s account:
• Go to Home
• Open Approval Centre
• Select Sales Order – Pending Approval
WFX Admin approves the Sales Order.
After the final approval, the Sales Order status becomes Confirmed, and this can be verified from the PO List.
Status Display
The Sales Order status will be clearly visible in the system, such as:
• Pending Approval
• Approved / Confirmed
• Rejected
The system will also display:
• Name of the Approver
• Approval / Rejection Status
• Approver Comments
• Date and Time of Action
This ensures complete visibility and tracking of the approval process.
Note:
All remarks entered during the approval process will be saved and updated in the History tab for tracking and audit purposes.

### Multiple Approval
To introduce a Multiple Approval option for Sales Order, allowing more than one approver to be assigned. This ensures that if one approver is unavailable, the other approver can approve the Sales Order without delay.
Multiple approvers can be assigned for Sales Order approval.
When multiple approvers are configured, a default approver can also be set. The default approver will be automatically displayed in the dropdown, while the remaining approvers will be available for selection within the dropdown list.
Permission Navigation
We need to introduce a new permission under Sales Order, which will include the following options:
• Sales Order – List
• Sales Order – New
In addition, in the last column, a view selection (dropdown/div option) should be provided.
This option will open the views created through the View Configurator, allowing the user to select a buyer-wise view.
Status Display
The Sales Order status will be clearly visible in the History, such as:
• Pending Approval
• Approved / Confirmed
• Rejected
The system will also display:
• Name of the Approver
• Approval / Rejection Status
• Approver Comments
• Date and Time of Action
This ensures complete visibility and tracking of the approval process.

## Actions Status

### Add Delivery
The Add Delivery option is a main function placed just above the delivery header in the Deliveries section.
A new delivery can be added in two ways:
• By clicking on the Add Delivery button from the main page.
• By clicking on the “+” (plus) icon is a primary action placed next to the Deliveries section in the left sidebar(This is present inside the pop-up screen present at the side of Deliveries Heading). This works only in the case of additional deliveries to be made, not for new/ Fresh delivery.
When We Click on “Add Delivery” for That Sales Order
*Note: Line Item column should be removed from the column level.
A detailed pop-up page opens
Behaviour for a Fully New Delivery
In the Left Sidebar:
• A new blank entry appears under the Deliveries section.
• It shows:
• Delivery – # _____ (blank)
• Style – ______ (blank)
• Both fields remain empty until the user fills and confirms the delivery.
In the Main Pop-up Page
The page contains two main sections:
• Delivery Information
• Article Information
For a completely new delivery:
• All fields are blank.
• All fields are editable.
• Some fields are mandatory and marked with “*” its need to shown as per Standard Angular UI.
• The user must fill the required fields before confirming.
When Creating a New Delivery Under the Same Sales Order
A New delivery under the same Sales Order can be created in two ways:
• By clicking the Add Delivery button from the main page.
• By clicking the “+” (plus) icon next to the Deliveries section in the left sidebar.
Both methods perform the same action.
What the System Does
When a new delivery is added:
• The delivery detail page opens.
• All fields are blank and editable for the new entry.
UI Behaviour:
• Previously created deliveries and styles remain visible in their original positions.
• Existing deliveries are not affected.
• Only the new delivery appears as a blank editable entry.
Left Sidebar Structure (Reference)
On the left side bar, the following details are shown:
• Header Section:
Sales Order Number is displayed at the top.
• Buyer Section:
Under the Sales Order Number:
• Buyer Name
• Order Value
• Deliveries Section
Below Buyer and Order Value, there is a Deliveries section where:
• All created deliveries are listed
• Each delivery shows:
• Delivery number
• Style code
A plus (+) icon is available next to the Deliveries header.
This icon allows adding a new delivery directly from the sidebar.
After Confirmation
Once the user fills all required details and clicks Confirm:
The blank delivery line is updated with:
• Delivery number
• Style
• Delivery date
• Line items
• Status
The status changes from Pending to Confirmed under Status header bar.
The delivery becomes part of the list under the Deliveries section.
Note: Transaction performed under this action is automatically logged in the History section.

### Copy Delivery
The Copy Delivery is a secondary option that is used to copy an already created delivery under the same sales order.
Copy Icon will be available in following areas:
• In the Main Delivery Table
• The Action column is placed next to the Status column.
• The Action bar at the header is right-pinned, meaning it stays fixed on the right side.
• Under this Action column, the Copy icon is available vertically for each delivery row.
• This allows copying a specific delivery directly from the table.
• In the Left Sidebar
• The Copy icon is also available on the side of particular deliveries shown.
When you click on copy
• A pop-up window opens.
• A new blank row appears in the deliveries section (at the left-most side).
In the new row
• Delivery number is blank.
• Style code is already present (copied from the selected delivery).
• Fields like delivery date, line, and style (prefilled) must be filled again by the user.
• All copied fields are editable so that the new delivery can be modified if needed.
After Confirmation
• The blank row gets updated with the entered details.
• A new line is added on the main page showing:
• Delivery
• Style
• Date
• Line items
• Status
The status changes from Pending to Confirmed, and the new delivery becomes active in the system.
Note: Transaction performed under this action is automatically logged in the History section.

### Delete action
When you click on the Delete option under the Action Status column for a particular delivery:
A confirmation pop-up appears stating “Are you sure you want to Remove Delivery” it need to be shown as per Angular standard.
When user delete multiple delivery at same time. A confirmation pop-up appears stating “Are you sure you want to Remove mentioned Delivery (Delivery 001, 002 & 003)” it need to be shown as per Angular standard.
By checking the checkbox you can delete multiple deliveries at a single time.
Note: Transaction performed under this action is automatically logged in the History section.

### Split action
When you click on the Split option under Action Status:
• A pop-up window appears.
• It shows only the delivery information.
You can split the delivery quantity in two ways:
• By Percentage (%) – It comes by default then add no. in text field. (toggled on)
• By Quantity – when you toggle off, split pop is shown like this.
On the header, only:
• Split Quantity
• Percentage will be shown (by default based on toggler`)
When you click on Split, the system performs the splitting action based on the method selected.
Splitting is possible from sidebar in Edit Sales order page.
While splitting a Save option will be present at the place of confirm to save the sales order changes.
Note: Transaction performed under this action is automatically logged in the History section.

### Cancel Action

#### Initial Step –
• First, the user views deliveries in non-editable mode.
• User can select single or multiple deliveries using checkboxes.
• User clicks on the context menu at the header level.
• Selects Cancel option.
• A popup appears to enter Remarks.
• User enters remarks and clicks Save and these remarks are shown in the history as well when user open the sales order delivery.
• After saving, the status changes from Confirmed to Cancelled in Red color.
• All of this is reflected in the UI as shown in the attached screenshot.

#### In editable mode-
1. Open Sales Order
• User opens an already created Sales Order.
• A Deliveries panel is displayed on the left side.
• The panel shows a list of all deliveries with checkboxes.
2. Select Delivery
• User can select:
• A single delivery, or
• Multiple deliveries using checkboxes.
3. Access Action Menu
• Click on the context menu in the Deliveries section.
• The following options are displayed:
• Reopen
• Close
• Cancel
4. Initiate Cancel Action
• User clicks on Cancel.
• A popup appears to capture Remarks.
5. Enter Remarks
• User enters remarks in the provided field.
• Remarks are required to proceed.
6. Save Remarks
• User clicks on the Save button.
7. Confirmation Prompt
• System displays a confirmation message:
"Do you want to Cancel the selected Delivery Order(s)?"
• Options available:
• OK → Proceed with cancellation
• Cancel → Abort the process
8. Successful Cancellation
• On clicking OK:
• The system cancels the selected delivery(s).
• A success message is displayed:
"Delivery OCs Cancel successfully."
9. Status Update
• The delivery status is updated to Cancelled.
• The updated status is displayed at the top of the page.
10. Remarks Display
• The entered remarks are:
• Saved in the system
• Displayed in the Remarks section for reference when you hover on it.
Note: Transaction performed under this action is automatically logged in the History section.

• A popup appears to enter Remarks.
• User enters remarks and clicks Save and these remarks are shown in the history as well when user open the sales order delivery.
• After saving, the status changes from Confirmed to Close in Orange color.

#### In editable mode-

• The following options are displayed:
• Open
• Close
• Cancel

• A popup appears to capture Remarks.
• Enter Remarks

• Remarks are required to proceed.
• Save Remarks

"Do you want to Close the selected Delivery Order(s)?"
• Options available:
• OK → Proceed with closing
• Cancel → Abort the process
• Status Update

• The updated status is displayed at the top of the page.

Note: Transaction performed under this action is automatically logged in the History section.

### Open (Re – Open) Action

#### Initial Step –
• First, the user views deliveries in non-editable mode and open action can only be done when the delivery is closed previously.
• User can select single or multiple deliveries using checkboxes.
• User clicks on the context menu at the header level.
• Selects Open (Re – Open) action.
• A popup appears to enter Remarks.
• User enters remarks and clicks Save.
• After saving, the status changes from Confirmed to Open in Green color.
• All of this is reflected in the UI as shown in the attached screenshot.

#### In editable mode-
• Open Sales Order
• User opens an already created Sales Order.
• Deliveries panel is visible on the left with list of deliveries and checkboxes.
• Select Delivery
• User selects single or multiple deliveries.
• Access Action Menu
• Click on context menu (⋮).
• Options available: Reopen, Close, Cancel.
• Perform Reopen Action
• Click on Reopen.
• Remarks popup appears → user enters remarks and clicks Save.
• Confirmation
• System shows message:
"Do you want to ReOpen the selected Delivery Order(s)?"
• Click OK to proceed or Cancel to abort.
• Successful Reopen
• Selected delivery(s) are reopened.
• Status changes from Closed → Open/Active.
• Delivery becomes editable again.
• Validation Case
• If delivery is not closed:
• System shows message:
"Please Uncheck Confirmed Delivery OC."
• Final Update
• Status is updated at the top of the page.
• Remarks are saved and visible in the Remarks section (on hover).
Note: Transaction performed under this action is automatically logged in the History section.

### History/Log section:
When we click on the History tab on the Add/Edit Sales Order page, it displays the complete activity details of that Sales Order.
The History section shows:
• Sales Order status updates
• Date and time of each action
• Username of the person who performed the action
It also includes:
• Approval trail (showing approver name and status such as Approved or Pending)
• Approver comments
• Comments and notes related to the Sales Order
In addition, the history will also capture delivery-level actions within the Sales Order activity logs.
For example:
Delivery order - <Event> - #<Delivery ID> - <Action Performed date & time> - <Action Performed by> - < Remarks>
Delivery Order Closed (1) 12:22:02 PM | 26/12/2026 Nishant Test Case [Sample Example]
This will display details such as:
• Delivery reference (Delivery number or name)
• Action performed on that delivery (e.g., Closed, Cancelled, Reopened)
• Corresponding date, time, and user details & remarks.

The BI Print action allows the user to generate and print the Sales Order details.

• After mapping this is the Navigation Impact:
Sales Order List -> Grid Level Context Menu -> BI Print -> Open Print BI Report
Print action works in non-editable mode.
Purpose of BI Print
• To create customized transaction reports.

Note: Data of the newly created Sales Order should also be saved in the stored procedures related to Purchase Order from Buyer.

## Desync Price OC List:
Setting Configuration:
Admin → Global Setup → Company Setup → Miscellaneous Settings
• Enable the setting:
“OC Price Validation with selling price in cost sheet” = ON
This setting ensures that the OC Selling Price is validated and picked from the Cost Sheet/ New BOM.
Navigation: (Current System Navigation)
Sales -> Purchase Order from buyer -> Desync Price OC list
In this screen, only the data created through the Cost Sheet/BOM will be visible.
Destination-wise pricing is defined in the Cost Sheet Summary / BOM.
Additional UI Enhancement (Sales Order List)
• In the Sales Order List screen, a Desync Tool icon should be provided for each Sales Order.
• The desync tool will be enabled only when there is selling price mismatch in the cost-sheet summary/New BOM and Sales Order.
• Along with the icon, a hyperlink should be available.
• On clicking this hyperlink, the system will open the OC Details screen.
1. Initial Cost Sheet Setup
Style 1 → Cost Sheet
For Destination India (IN), the selling price is set as 10 in the Cost Sheet.
2. OC Creation – Manual Price Entry (Desync Scenario)
When creating an OC (Order Confirmation):
• Select Style 1
• Select Destination India (IN)
• User manually enters Selling Price in OC as:
20 INR
This creates a desync condition, where:
• Cost Sheet/BOM Price = 10
• OC Price = 20
3. Desync Trigger Condition
• If the user changes the Selling Price either:
• In Cost Sheet / BOM, or
• In OC (Order Confirmation)
• The system will mark the record as Desynced and in Blue Color.
4. Sync Action using Desync Tool
• User clicks on the Desync Tool icon from the Sales Order List.
• System will:
• Status changes to Sync and in Green color.
• Fetch the latest Selling Price from Cost Sheet / BOM
• Override the OC Selling Price
• Example:
OC Price: 20 → 10
The final price will always be taken from the Cost Sheet / BOM (source of truth).
5. OC Details View
On clicking the hyperlink, system opens OC Details screen
The screen displays:
• Destination
• Delivery Date
• Color / Size
• OC Selling Price
• Cost Sheet/BOM Selling Price
6. Price Display & Validation
• OC Selling Price / Customer Price is shown per line item
• Cost Sheet/BOM Selling Price is shown alongside
• Pricing is maintained destination-wise
• System ensures correct mapping after sync

### Key Logic
• Any mismatch between OC and Cost Sheet/BOM price triggers desync
• Sync action always aligns OC price with Cost Sheet/BOM price only

## BOM Information access via Context menu:
On clicking the context menu, the user will see an option named “BOM Information.”
Upon clicking over this option BOM of style will be opened that is being attached in that particular delivery but only in view mode.

## Delivery Update:

Access from UI (Header Level)

• Click on the context menu → Select Delivery Updates option.
• The menu name will be updated as “Sales Order” (currently displayed as Summary OC).
Editable Fields
In the Sales Order – Delivery Update screen, the following fields are editable:
• Buyer Delivery Date
• OC Delivery Date
• Buyer Order Date
• PCD Date
• PO Packet Date
• GAC Date
Update Process
• The user can modify the required editable fields directly in the grid.
• After making the necessary changes, click on Save.
System Behaviour After Save
• Once saved, the system will update the edited fields.
• The updated values will be reflected in:
• The respective OC (Order Confirmation)
• The related transaction screens
Validation
After updating and saving:
• Verify that the modified dates are correctly updated in the OC.
• Ensure that the latest saved data is visible across all relevant sections.

## EDI Buyer PO:
EDI Buyer PO is an electronically transmitted Purchase Order received from the buyer’s system through Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) and automatically processed in WFX ERP to create a Buyer Purchase Order based on predefined mapping, validation, and business rules.
The benefits of EDI:
• It saves time.
• Reduce manual errors.
• Faster order execution.
• Improves data accuracy.
Before creating an EDI Buyer PO, the following configurations must be completed:
• Package Configuration
• Package Mapping

### Package Configuration:
Package Configuration is an administrative setup used to define and manage EDI integration packages that control how EDI transactions are processed within the system.
Path: Admin Integration Package Configuration
In this screen user can fill the required fields to configure the packages while adding new configuration by clicking on Add button and the fields are as follows:
• Company: Company for which EDI integration is configured.
• Package Company Division: It shows all selected company divisions.
• Entity Type: Defines the entity level at which the transaction is processed.
• Company
• Buyer
• Supplier
• Transaction Type: Specifies the type of EDI transaction such as Buyer PO, TechPack, Sales Order or BOM.
• Package Type: Package Type defines the direction of data flow between an external system (Buyer/Supplier) and WFX ERP during EDI integration.
• Import - Data is received from an external system into WFX ERP.
• Export - Data is sent from WFX ERP to an external system.
• SSIS Package: Backend integration package responsible for processing and executing EDI data transactions.
• Standard Package Name: Standard reference name used by the system for package identification and processing.
• Folder Path: File location from where EDI data files are picked or stored for processing.
• Article: Defines the applicable article for the transaction, if required.
• Purchase Officer: Assigned responsible user for the package configuration (optional).
• Active: Enables or disables the package for EDI transaction processing.
After filling all the details, we have to save the configuration by clicking on Save button.
If we want to delete the configuration, we can do that by clicking on Delete button.

### Package Mapping:
Package Mapping is used to define the mapping between incoming EDI package data and fields required for processing Buyer Orders. It ensures that data received through EDI is correctly interpreted and linked with system fields before creating transactions.
Path: Admin Integration Package Mapping
In the Process Mapping screen, users configure the mapping logic for EDI transactions. The system displays mapping fields based on the selected Package Type and Package, allowing users to map EDI data elements with corresponding Buyer Order fields.
This configuration enables accurate data transformation and successful creation of EDI Buyer Purchase Orders.
For mapping first select package type and package which are configured in package configuration.
After selecting both, the mapped fields are visible. Each row represents a WFX transaction field and defines how its value will be populated during EDI Buyer PO processing.
In that screen, there are different columns as follows:
• WFX Field: Displays the target field where the EDI data will be stored during Buyer PO creation.
• Package Field: Represents the source field received from the EDI package which will populate the corresponding field.
• Mapping Resolution Type: Defines how the system assigns or resolves the value for the field during EDI processing. The available values are:
• Data: System automatically takes the value directly from the EDI file when mapping exists.
• System Data: Value is derived automatically from system configuration or master data.
• User Input: User manually enters the value during transaction processing.
• Review & Create: User reviews the incoming value and creates a new master record if it does not exist.
• Review & Map: User maps the incoming EDI value with an existing master value.
• Review & Resolve: User reviews and corrects mismatched data before processing continues.
• Review & Select: User selects the appropriate value from available system options.
• Dependent On Field Name: Specifies the parent or related field on which the current field depends for validation or value derivation.
• Mandatory: Indicates whether the field is compulsory for successful Buyer PO creation.
• Transaction Visibility: Defines whether the field will be visible during transaction processing.
• Editable: Determines whether the mapped value can be modified by the user after processing.
• Sort Order: Defines the sequence in which fields appear during transaction processing.
After completing the mapping configuration, the user must save the setup by clicking on the Save button.

### EDI Buyer PO creation:
Path: Sales Purchase Order from Buyer EDI Buyer PO
After navigating to the EDI Buyer PO path, the EDI Buyer PO screen is displayed. This screen is used to import buyer purchase order data received through EDI and convert it into Buyer Orders within WFX ERP.
The screen allows the user to select the required Buyer and configured Package, which determines the mapping and processing logic for the incoming EDI data.
Import Functionality
To initiate the EDI Buyer PO creation process, the user selects the desired Buyer and Package and clicks on the Import button. This action starts the file import process for the selected configuration.
File Selection
Upon clicking Import, the system prompts the user to select the EDI file from the local system. The user selects the required Excel file containing buyer order data and proceeds with the upload.
Process Package
After selecting the file, the user clicks on Process Package. The system reads the uploaded file, validates the data based on configured mappings and business rules, and prepares the data for transaction creation.
During this stage, the system checks mandatory fields, mapping configurations, and master data validations.
Error Resolution
If any mapping mismatch or validation error is identified during processing, the records are routed to the Error Resolution stage.
After Process Package, the uploaded file visible in Error Resolution, and it is accessible from the
In the Error Resolution screen, the user reviews and resolves issues such as:
• Missing master data
• Incorrect mappings
• Unrecognized values
• Validation failures
After resolving all errors, the records become eligible for transaction creation.
Pending and Create Transaction
Once error resolution is completed, the processed records appear in the Pending stage. The user reviews the data and clicks on Create Transaction or Pending to generate Buyer Orders in the system.
This step converts the imported EDI data into actual Buyer Order transactions in WFX ERP.
Tabs and Transaction Status
After creating the transaction, the EDI Buyer PO records are categorized into different tabs based on their processing status. These tabs help users manage Buyer Orders during different stages of validation and processing.
New Tab:
Displays newly created Buyer Orders imported through EDI. These orders are available for review and validation before confirmation.
Revision Tab:
Displays Buyer Orders that are updated through EDI import where existing orders are modified. Users can review the revised information before processing.
On Hold Tab:
Displays orders that are manually placed on hold by the user to delay confirmation or further processing by clicking OnHold Button.
And from this we can also Unhold the Buyer order by clicking on Unhold Button.
Processed Tab:
Displays Buyer Orders that have been confirmed and successfully processed by the system.
Delivery Level View:
From the transaction tabs, users can open the Buyer Order by clicking the available hyperlink under Delivery Detail column. This opens the Delivery Level View, where order information is displayed shipment-wise or delivery-wise.
The screen allows users to review delivery details such as delivery dates, quantities, and associated shipment information before final confirmation.
Color / Size Level View:
Within the Delivery Level View, users can further drill down to the Color and Size Level details.
This view displays the detailed breakup of ordered quantities based on color and size combinations, allowing users to validate item-level information received through EDI
Confirm Functionality
After reviewing delivery and color-size details, users can confirm the Buyer Order using the Confirm Button.
Confirmation finalizes the transaction and converts the EDI data into an active Buyer Order within the system.
Export Functionality
The Export option allows users to download or view the processed EDI transaction data file for reference, validation, or external sharing purposes.

## MRL Related changes:
When the user selects the Order Type as ‘CM’ in Sales Order, the system shall automatically generate a GMPO (Garment Purchase Order) against the corresponding final product indent.
Under this scenario, the MRP (Material Requirement Planning) logic shall be enhanced to ensure that all purchase demands linked to the final product are automatically fulfilled by the system. The demand generation and allocation will be system-driven, without requiring any manual intervention.
Additionally, once the purchase demand is created through this process, it shall be locked for editing. Users will not be allowed to modify, override, or delete the auto-fulfilled demand, ensuring data consistency and adherence to the defined process flow.
CM Order – Pricing Enhancement
• In case of CM type orders, the system should capture and use Purchase Price instead of Selling Price for GMPO generation.
UI Changes
1. Color Level
• A new column “Purchase Price” should be added adjacent to Selling Price.
• Purchase Price will be entered row-wise (per color).
• The field should be manually editable.
2. Size Level
• A new row “Purchase Price” should be added below Selling Price.
• Purchase Price will be entered column-wise (per size).
• The field should be manually editable.
Logic Correction
• Currently, the Selling Price is being picked as GMPO price, which is incorrect.
• The system should instead pick Purchase Price as GMPO price for CM orders.
• Purchase Price can be entered manually as well on sales order.

## Material Requirement Status via Context Menu:
On clicking the context menu, the user will see an option named “Material Requirement Status.”
MR Status Report -> Material Status Pop- up opens for that particular style present in that delivery.

• When a TNA template is attached, a different icon will be displayed to indicate that TNA is already configured.

- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO:): EDI Buyer PO is an electronically transmitted Purchase Order received from the buyer’s system through Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) and automatically processed in WFX ERP to create a Buyer Purchase Order based on predefined mapping, validation, and business rules.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO:): EDI Buyer PO is an electronically transmitted Purchase Order received from the buyer’s system through Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) and automatically processed in WFX ERP to create a Buyer Purchase Order based on predefined mapping, validation, and business rules.
- workflow_steps (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO:): EDI Buyer PO:: / 1. It saves time. / 2. Reduce manual errors. / 3. Faster order execution. / 4. Improves data accuracy.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO:): Before creating an EDI Buyer PO, the following configurations must be completed:
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Configuration:): Package Configuration is an administrative setup used to define and manage EDI integration packages that control how EDI transactions are processed within the system.
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Configuration:): Import - Data is received from an external system into WFX ERP.
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Configuration:): Export - Data is sent from WFX ERP to an external system.
- workflow_steps (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Configuration:): Package Configuration:: / 1. Company: Company for which EDI integration is configured. / 2. Package Company Division: It shows all selected company divisions. / 3. Entity Type: Defines the entity level at which the transaction is processed. / 4. Company / 5. Buyer / 6. Supplier / 7. Transaction Type: Specifies the type of EDI transaction such as Buyer PO, TechPack, Sales Order or BOM. / 8. Package Type: Package Type defines the direction of data flow between an external system (Buyer/Supplier) and WFX ERP during EDI integration. / 9. Import - Data is received from an external system into WFX ERP. / 10. Export - Data is sent from WFX ERP to an external system. / 11. SSIS Package: Backend integration package responsible for processing and executing EDI data transactions. / 12. Standard Package Name: Standard reference name used by the system for package identification and processing. / 13. Folder Path: File location from where EDI data files are picked or stored for processing. / 14. Article: Defines the applicable article for the transaction, if required. / 15. Purchase Officer: Assigned responsible user for the package configuration (optional). / 16. Active: Enables or disables the package for EDI transaction processing.
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Mapping:): Package Mapping is used to define the mapping between incoming EDI package data and fields required for processing Buyer Orders.
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Mapping:): It ensures that data received through EDI is correctly interpreted and linked with system fields before creating transactions.
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Mapping:): For mapping first select package type and package which are configured in package configuration.
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Mapping:): Each row represents a WFX transaction field and defines how its value will be populated during EDI Buyer PO processing.
- formula (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Mapping:): System Data: Value is derived automatically from system configuration or master data.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Mapping:): Dependent On Field Name: Specifies the parent or related field on which the current field depends for validation or value derivation.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Mapping:): Mandatory: Indicates whether the field is compulsory for successful Buyer PO creation.
- workflow_steps (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Mapping:): Package Mapping:: / 1. WFX Field: Displays the target field where the EDI data will be stored during Buyer PO creation. / 2. Package Field: Represents the source field received from the EDI package which will populate the corresponding field. / 3. Mapping Resolution Type: Defines how the system assigns or resolves the value for the field during EDI processing. The available values are: / 4. Data: System automatically takes the value directly from the EDI file when mapping exists. / 5. System Data: Value is derived automatically from system configuration or master data. / 6. User Input: User manually enters the value during transaction processing. / 7. Review & Create: User reviews the incoming value and creates a new master record if it does not exist. / 8. Review & Map: User maps the incoming EDI value with an existing master value. / 9. Review & Resolve: User reviews and corrects mismatched data before processing continues. / 10. Review & Select: User selects the appropriate value from available system options. / 11. Dependent On Field Name: Specifies the parent or related field on which the current field depends for validation or value derivation. / 12. Mandatory: Indicates whether the field is compulsory for successful Buyer PO creation. / 13. Transaction Visibility: Defines whether the field will be visible during transaction processing. / 14. Editable: Determines whether the mapped value can be modified by the user after processing. / 15. Sort Order: Defines the sequence in which fields appear during transaction processing.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › Package Mapping:): After completing the mapping configuration, the user must save the setup by clicking on the Save button.
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): This screen is used to import buyer purchase order data received through EDI and convert it into Buyer Orders within WFX ERP.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): The system reads the uploaded file, validates the data based on configured mappings and business rules, and prepares the data for transaction creation.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): During this stage, the system checks mandatory fields, mapping configurations, and master data validations.
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): If any mapping mismatch or validation error is identified during processing, the records are routed to the Error Resolution stage.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): If any mapping mismatch or validation error is identified during processing, the records are routed to the Error Resolution stage.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): Validation failures
- workflow_steps (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): EDI Buyer PO creation:: / 1. Missing master data / 2. Incorrect mappings / 3. Unrecognized values / 4. Validation failures
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): Once error resolution is completed, the processed records appear in the Pending stage.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): These tabs help users manage Buyer Orders during different stages of validation and processing.
- definition (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): These orders are available for review and validation before confirmation.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): These orders are available for review and validation before confirmation.
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): This view displays the detailed breakup of ordered quantities based on color and size combinations, allowing users to validate item-level information received through EDI
- validation (§ Solution › EDI Buyer PO: › EDI Buyer PO creation:): The Export option allows users to download or view the processed EDI transaction data file for reference, validation, or external sharing purposes.
